properties.foundation_analysis: The subterranean geology of Marchmont rests upon the Upper Oil-Shale and Gullane Formations of the Carboniferous sedimentary sequence, overlain by dense glacial till. The superstructures are constructed predominantly of indigenous Lower Carboniferous quartz sandstones, featuring pale grey-buff and carbon-flecked laminated stone extracted from Hailes and Craigleith quarries, alongside Permo-Triassic New Red/Locharbriggs sandstones deployed in late Victorian phases. Mortar chemistry consists of traditional lime mortar binders (slaked hydraulic lime with sharp quartz river sand aggregate) providing essential vapor permeability. Natural subterranean drainage flows northwards down the glacial slope toward the historic Burgh Loch basin (The Meadows).

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Urban temperate vegetation in rear courtyard plots and sidewalk verges. Mature leafy canopy of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), and *Betula pendula* (Silver Birch), displaying organic deciduous branching, deep green serrated foliage, and natural irregular crowns distinct from building masonry.

properties.architectural_summary:
Classic late-Victorian Scottish Baronial / Renaissance revival tenement blocks (c. 1876–1890) flanking the junction of Marchmont Crescent, Roseneath Street, and Warrender Park Road. 
- **Typology & Height:** Solid four-to-five-storey load-bearing masonry blocks (16–20m elevation to ridge) above raised plinths and ground-floor commercial units.
- **Corner Features & Articulation:** Prominent corner conical turrets (tourelles) with corbelled ashlar bases, crow-stepped and pedimented nepus gables, decorative stringcourses, and heavy ashlar wallhead chimney stacks with terracotta chimney pots.
- **Fenestration:** Rectilinear vertical timber sash-and-case windows (one-over-one and two-over-two patterns) recessed in crisp, roll-moulded stone reveals.
- **Planar Rectification:** All exterior load-bearing ashlar and snecked rubble walls are plumbed to absolute gravitational vertical; horizontal stringcourses, lead roof valleys, and Ballachulish slate pitched roof planes are rectified into true planar geometries.
